clue.text: Way a pharmacist emulates a butterfly? Just so

definitions.note: a verb phrase: in a Kipling Just So story a butterfly brings its foot down hard to impress its wife

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualified chemist

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a chemist's route imitates a butterfly's flight, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just so' points to Kipling's Just So Stories, where the tale 'The Butterfly that ...' has a butterfly bringing its foot down to scare everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's children's tale a butterfly thumps its foot on the ground, so to imitate it is to bring a foot down hard.

clue.text: Very bad description of an early year

definitions.meaning: a toddler's second year of life is known as the '... twos', a time of tantrums

explanation.surface: An awful account of someone's first years.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost its last word 'year', clear on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful or dreadful is very bad, and toddlers' tantrum-prone age two is famously called the ... twos.

clue.text: Offences spelt out in spymasters' documents

explanation.surface: Crimes listed in the papers of intelligence chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelt out in' just links: the answer reads as MI's deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoings and crimes are offences.

clue.text: Resentment following second tax rise in Norway

explanation.definitionFit: The port city on Norway's south-west coast is a place in that country.

clue.text: Coxcomb's invitation to bird to pay a visit

explanation.surface: A dandy invites a bird to drop round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invitation to bird' reads as 'Pop in, jay!', the invitation spoken to the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb and a popinjay are both old words for a vain, showy fop.

clue.text: Student in US jail accepts airman as special envoy

indicators.note: the jail accepts, takes inside, the airman

explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat given full powers to act for a government is an envoy with special authority.

clue.text: Arraign one representative per capita

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP is a member of parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: Indict a single politician on a per head basis.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a public official formally with misconduct is to arraign them.

clue.text: Desert rat held the ring with Montgomery initially, showing lots of bottle

clue.text: Long endlessly to reserve this publication

indicators.note: endlessly means losing the final letter

explanation.surface: Wanting endlessly to reserve a copy of a magazine.

clue.text: A period on deck training horses

explanation.surface: A spell on a ship's deck spent schooling horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck but is the verb to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The equestrian discipline of schooling a horse to perform precise movements is a form of horse training.

clue.text: Harsh environment a setback for a group of drummers

explanation.surface: A tough place proves a setback for a band's percussion section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns round A TRAPS; traps is jazz slang for a drum kit.

clue.text: Illuminated age? Too indistinct at first for the well-read

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A question about an enlightened epoch, then a complaint that something is too blurry for scholars.

clue.text: Tree identified by scholar, ex-pupil and naval rating

AB is an able seaman, a naval rating

explanation.surface: A tree is spotted by an academic, a former schoolboy and a sailor.

clue.text: Not an ornament, though, when it comes to the crunch

definitions.text: Not an ornament, though, when it comes to the crunch

explanation.surface: Something is denied to be decorative when it really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is an architectural ornament, which is why the clue says 'not an ornament'; 'crunch' means biting, the jaw of a canine.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed canine tooth of a hound does the biting rather than decorating a Norman arch.

clue.text: Marine fossil, one in brittle round formation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

clue.text: A group of servicemen writing about French art

explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb form 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Servicemen who eat together form a dining group sharing a hall, the officers' or sergeants'.

clue.text: Wait under sea to give support

clue.text: Notedly detached censor upholds mounting of show

clue.text: Claim to be fit, though in a murderous frenzy

clue.text: Liqueur is an eye-opener in taste, perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IN TASTE to ANISETT, then E (eye's opener) follows.

clue.text: To Dido, no resort like 13, in a sense

clue.text: Language of a heretic taking people in

clue.text: A married woman is continent

parts.note: Erica is a woman's name
